examples.en: The teacher encouraged the students before their exam.
My friend cheered me up when I was having a hard time.
Encouraging team members is also part of a team leader's job.
We encouraged each other and ran the marathon to the end.
The boss gave words of encouragement to the staff.

examples.ko: 실패한 후배를 격려할 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a way to encourage my junior who failed.

explain: 격려하다는 힘이 빠진 사람에게 용기를 주는 말과 행동이에요. 친구끼리는 '응원하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, 격려하다는 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 하는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 격려하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 격려하다 means to give courage to someone who is down. Friends usually say 응원하다 (cheer on), while 격려하다 often sounds like a senior speaking to a junior. It takes an object: '~을/를 격려하다'.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 어릴 때부터 제 단짝이에요.
examples.en: That friend has been my best buddy since we were little.
I ended up in the same class as my best friend.
We two are famous at school as a duo.
I fought with my best friend and I feel bad.
I want to meet a close friend at my new school.
A close friend understands you without words.

explain: '단짝'은 늘 둘이 붙어 다니는 사이라서 보통 한 명을 말해요. '베프'는 '베스트 프렌드'를 줄인 젊은 말투이고, '절친'은 '절친한 친구'를 줄인 말이에요.
explain_en: 단짝 is someone you are always with, so it usually points to one person. 베프 is a young-sounding short form of 'best friend', and 절친 is a short form of 절친한 친구 (a very close friend).

examples.en: I feel hurt because no one understands how I feel.
Why don't you recognize my efforts?

examples.ko: 그녀는 남자가 자기 마음을 몰라주는 게 못내 섭섭했어요.
examples.en: She felt sad that the man didn't understand her feelings.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 사정을 몰라줄 때 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was upset when my friend didn't understand my situation.
I hoped he would recognize it, but he never did.

examples.ko: 엄마는 내 고생을 몰라주는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems my mom doesn't appreciate how hard I've worked.

explain: '알아주다'의 반대로, 내 마음이나 노력, 사정을 상대가 이해하거나 인정해 주지 않을 때 써요. 단순히 모르는 게 아니라 '알아줬으면 하는데 안 알아준다'는 서운한 느낌이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '알아주다', used when someone doesn't understand or acknowledge your feelings, effort or situation. It isn't just not knowing; it carries a hurt feeling of 'I wish you had recognized this, but you didn't'.

examples.en: I had a hard time because of my friend's betrayal.
That movie is a story of love and betrayal.

examples.ko: 가장 믿던 사람의 배반을 겪으면 마음이 무너져요.
examples.en: When the person you trusted most betrays you, your heart breaks.

examples.ko: 회사를 위해 일했는데 돌아온 건 배반이었어요.
examples.en: I worked for the company, and what I got back was betrayal.

examples.ko: 역사책에는 왕에 대한 신하의 배반이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: History books often mention a minister's betrayal of the king.
Betrayal is hard to forgive easily.

explain: '배신'과 뜻이 거의 같아요. '배반'은 믿음이나 약속을 어기고 등을 돌린다는 느낌이 강해서 나라·조직·역사 이야기에도 잘 어울려요. 친구에게 말할 때는 '배신당했어'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Nearly the same as '배신'. '배반' strongly suggests breaking trust or a promise and turning one's back, so it fits stories about countries, organizations and history. To a friend, '배신당했어' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 그 수학자는 오랫동안 어려운 문제를 풀었어요.
examples.en: That mathematician worked on a hard problem for a long time.
My dream is to become a mathematician.
I met a famous mathematician and listened to what they had to say.
The mathematicians gathered and held a meeting.
My uncle is a mathematician, so he loves numbers.
I sent a letter directly to a mathematician.

explain: '-자'는 학문을 하는 사람 뒤에 붙어요. 수학자, 과학자, 철학자처럼요. 학교에서 수학을 가르치는 사람은 '수학 선생님'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: The ending '-자' attaches to people who work in a field of study, as in 수학자, 과학자, and 철학자. Someone who teaches math at school is called a '수학 선생님'.

en: get divorced; be divorced from; be separated by divorce

examples.en: My parents divorced when I was little.
I heard that couple decided to divorce.
After the divorce, she started new work.
I asked why they want to divorce.
My friend's parents got divorced and live separately.
I worried about how to live if I divorced.

explain: '이혼하다'는 '~와/과 이혼하다'로 쓰고 결혼한 사이에서만 말해요. 사귀는 사이에서 헤어지는 것은 '헤어지다'예요. 'ㅎ' 때문에 [이호나다]로 소리 나요.
explain_en: 이혼하다 is used as '~와/과 이혼하다' and only for married couples. For a couple that is dating, use 헤어지다. Because of ㅎ, it is pronounced [이호나다].

examples.ko: 청년기에 겪은 경험이 평생 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Experiences in young adulthood affect you for life.
Most people worry a lot about their career path in young adulthood.
That writer spent his youth abroad.
Health habits from young adulthood carry into old age.
It's fascinating to hear stories of my grandfather's youth.

examples.ko: 청년기와 장년기는 몸 상태가 많이 달라요.
examples.en: Physical condition is very different in young adulthood and middle age.

explain: 사람의 삶을 나눌 때 '유아기, 청소년기, 청년기, 장년기, 노년기'처럼 나오는 시기 이름이에요. 청소년기 다음, 어른이 되어 가는 시기를 말해요. 글이나 수업에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: This is a life-stage name seen in lists like '유아기, 청소년기, 청년기, 장년기, 노년기'. It means the period after the teen years, when one becomes an adult. You often see it in texts and lessons.

examples.en: Even after marriage, I call my father often.
My father sent me kimchi.
My father farms in the countryside.
It's my father's birthday, so I'm going down this weekend.
I'm tall because I take after my father.
I left my child with my father and went to work.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 아버지를 말할 때 써요. 남편의 아버지는 '시아버지', 남자가 아내의 아버지를 말할 때는 '장인어른'이라고 해요. 결혼 전의 딸이 말할 때는 그냥 '아버지'를 써요.
explain_en: A married woman uses this for her own father. Her husband's father is '시아버지', and a man calls his wife's father '장인어른'. An unmarried daughter would simply say '아버지'.

examples.ko: 그 커플은 결혼식 한 달 전에 파혼했어요.
examples.en: That couple broke off their engagement a month before the wedding.
Our values were too different, so we decided to call off the engagement.
I heard the news that my friend suddenly broke off her engagement.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 두 사람은 오해 때문에 파혼해요.
examples.en: In the drama, the two break off their engagement because of a misunderstanding.
If you break off the engagement, what happens to the wedding hall fee?
We almost broke off the engagement because of my parents' objection.

explain: 약혼이나 결혼 약속을 깼을 때 써요. 이미 결혼한 사이가 헤어지는 것은 '이혼하다'라고 해요. 한 사람이 일방적으로 깰 때는 '파혼을 통보하다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when an engagement or a promise to marry is broken. For couples already married, the word is '이혼하다' (divorce). When one side does it alone, people say '파혼을 통보하다' (announce the break-off).

examples.en: I made up with the friend I fought with yesterday.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 화해하는 장면에서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried at the scene where the two people make up.
I want to apologize first and make up with my younger sibling.

examples.ko: 사이가 나빴던 두 나라가 화해해서 다시 무역을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The two countries that had been on bad terms reconciled and started trading again.
Shall we make up now?

examples.ko: 부모님과 화해하려면 먼저 마음을 열어야 해요.
examples.en: To make up with your parents, you first have to open your heart.

explain: 싸운 뒤에 다시 사이가 좋아질 때 써요. 한쪽이 사과하고 다른 쪽이 받아 주면 화해하게 돼요. 'A와 화해하다'처럼 '와/과'와 같이 써요. 반대는 '다투다'예요. 가볍게는 '마음을 풀다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when people become friendly again after a fight. It happens when one side apologizes and the other accepts. It goes with the particle 와/과, as in 'A와 화해하다'. The opposite is 다투다. In a lighter way people also say '마음을 풀다'.
